newsitem.title: USA: Miami city manager threatens to fire top leaders.
newsitem.headline: Miami city manager threatens to fire top leaders.

text.p: Miami City Manager Ed Marquez issued a memo Friday telling top city workers they risk losing their jobs unless they "get on the bandwagon" and help change the entrenched fiscal culture that led to the city's $68 million deficit.
The memo was sent to six assistant city managers and 17 department heads and said they had until mid-March to "join the team."
"Those whose actions say they want to stay will be ask to do so," Marquez wrote in the letter.
Marquez, a former Dade County finance director, was hired as Miami City Manager amid the city's struggle to close the $68 million gap in its $275 million budget for the year that began Oct. 1.

The city, which is now operating under the watchful eye of a state oversight board, has spent more than it takes in for years but did not acknowledge the deficit until after three top officials resigned to face federal corruption charges.
